observations: body L1-L3: the end of aṣ-Ṣūfī's quotation begun on p. 297. The o of «rapporte» (L3) prints broken, and a point between «de» and «la» (L3) is a speck.
body L4-L5: «aṣ–Ṣūfī» (L4) is not letter-spaced; its long dash measures 5.5 pt.
body L6-L8: a speck stands before «Ad caput LII.»; the dash after «a)» measures 10.0 pt.

body L9-L24: «Ptolemaeus» and «Theon Alexandrinus», divided between L9 and L10, and «Ptolemaeo» (L14) are letter-spaced; the dashes after «I.» (L9), before «quod» (L13), before «rationem» (L16) and before «Nam» (L17) measure 10.2, 10.3, 10.1 and 9.5 pt. The Greek is set as printed: «τροπῆς», «κατά», with an acute on its final α, «παλαιοὶ», «ἀποτελεσματικῶν» and «παραινοῦμεν». In Theon's reckoning the trepidation, from its greatest eastward digression of 8° at 128 years before Augustus, at 1° in 80 years, has gone back 8° in 640 years, so that it must be reversed and taken from 8° when the quotient exceeds 8.

body L25-L34: «Theonis», «Al–Battānī», «Thābit ibn Qurrah», «Ibn Yūnus», «Caussin» and «Theon» (L32) are letter-spaced; «Al–Battānī» and «al–aḥkām» have long dashes (5.4 and 5.5 pt). The year 288 of the Hiǵrah ran from 26 December 900 to 15 December 901 (Julian, by the tabular calendar).
notes_left L1-L4: the Greek of Theon, Handy Tables, ed. Halma t. I, p. 53, is set as printed: «συμφωνειν» and «ταις» without accents, «καταλήψεσιν» with the iota of the η printed apart, like a comma.
notes_left L5-L8: «Delambre», «Letronnii» and «Martinii» are letter-spaced; the closing parenthesis of «(2)» prints broken, and «625-27» has a hyphen (2.5 pt).
notes_right L1-L4: «Abhrāhām bar Ḥiyyā», divided between L1 and L2, and «Albatenii» are letter-spaced; «Hebraeo-Hispanus» has a hyphen (2.8 pt). A point below the i of «ignotam» (L3) is a speck.

notes_right L5-L7: «Suter» is letter-spaced. The closing parenthesis of «(4)» did not print; a gap of its width stands before «Obiit». The ‘ of «rabī‘» prints as a raised point. «39–40» has a long dash (4.3 pt). The month Rabī‘ II of 298 of the Hiǵrah ran from 7 December 910 to 4 January 911 (Julian, by the tabular calendar), at the end of 910, as printed.
